title: Instances are pre-registered as Active with their risk envelope set before the contracts exist
content:
The Arbitrum Spark Savings v2 USDT instance is filed under `Active` and carries a complete risk configuration — "Supply cap: 250,000,000 USDT, Max yield: 6%, Current yield (at launch): 0%" (A.6.1.1.1.2.6.1.3.3.3.1.4.2.1) — while three of its addresses read "TBD": the `Token Address` (.1.2.2.1), the `Spark Vault v2 Implementation` (.1.4.1.1) and the `Setter` (.1.4.1.3). Only the Default admin and the Taker are populated. The two Binance conduits show the same shape: full limits, deposit address TBD.

Read together these are not oversights but a workflow. The governance-relevant decisions — how large the product may become, what it may pay, which operations are unbounded — are taken and published first; the deployment artefacts are filled in afterwards. Approval precedes existence.

The sizing confirms the envelope is genuinely deliberated rather than copied: 250,000,000 USDT at 6% max yield on Arbitrum against 4,000,000,000 at 10% for the mainnet USDT product. Someone decided this chain warrants a sixteenth of the capacity and a lower rate ceiling.

The cost is that `Active` stops meaning operational. Across this Artifact the same label now covers live venues, ceiling-suppressed venues, venues awaiting a deposit address, and one product whose vault contract does not yet have an address. The status field marks governance approval; operability has to be reconstructed from whether the parameters are populated and non-zero — which is exactly the reading a summary of the `Active` set would skip.
description: The Arbitrum savings vault publishes a 250,000,000 USDT supply cap and 6% max yield while its Token Address, vault implementation and Setter all read TBD
